children.text: What is play? What does it do for us?

From childhood make-believe and theatre to sports and market speculation, play takes many forms: it offers entertainment and leisure while giving people a way to explore the world and its possibilities through imagined or constructed settings. It is a fundamental aspect of how we interact with the world. Play can have many participants. Play can involve many participants. We play with objects, with our thoughts, with fellow humans--friends, loved ones, and strangers. We also play with other life forms. There are many theories of play. Play is often described as practice: a way to develop physical skills, learn social cues, or encounter the unexpected in a relatively safe setting. These explanations offer a functional reading of play, but they don’t settle the question of how do we play?
There is a certain ambiguity to play. “Play” is a useful analytical category, precisely because it’s hard to pin down. There is no specific. Play vary so much in the human world.

In animals, it often looks like a familiar action—chasing, wrestling, pouncing, handling an object—but performed in a way that is relaxed, voluntary, varied, and not serving its usual immediate purpose.

title: Multi-species Play: Sea lion interactions in La Ventana, Mexico
